definitions.explanation: Physical injury or harm to the body. Used in both general and medical contexts.
In legal contexts, the crime of deliberately causing physical injury to another person. A key term in Japanese criminal law.

examples.english: I sustained injuries in the accident.

notes:
An important word with both general and legal uses. In everyday use it refers to physical injury; in news and legal contexts it refers to the crime of assault causing bodily harm.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {傷害|しょうがい}{罪|ざい}: crime of assault, assault charge
- {傷害|しょうがい}⟦{事件|じけん}→事件：01568_jiken⟧: assault case
- {傷害|しょうがい}{保険|ほけん}: injury insurance, accident insurance
- {傷害|しょうがい}⟦{致死|ちし}→致死：10002_chishi⟧: assault resulting in death
- {傷害|しょうがい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{負|お}う→負う：02017_ou⟧: to sustain an injury

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{障害|しょうがい}→障害：03228_shougai⟧: disability; obstacle — same pronunciation but different kanji and meaning
- ⟦{負傷|ふしょう}→負傷：15287_fushou⟧: injury, wound — similar to sense 1 but more commonly used for wounds from accidents or combat
- ⟦{暴行|ぼうこう}→暴行：27862_boukou⟧: assault, violence — the act of violence itself, regardless of whether injury results

USAGE:
Careful not to confuse with ⟦{障害|しょうがい}→障害：03228_shougai⟧ (disability/obstacle), which is a homophone. The kanji {傷|しょう} (wound) versus {障|しょう} (barrier) distinguishes them in writing.
